analysis:
This PR changes documentation only. docs/reference/configuration.md line 379 now documents DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and expands lines 380-381 for STEP_TOKENS and SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE. It also adds a new report, docs/reports/2026-10-21-mixed-step-prefill-geometry.md, and an index entry in docs/reports/README.md. No source code, key handling, attestation, coordinator WebSocket, or prefix-cache storage logic changes.

I checked the documented behavior against the threat model. Larger prefill chunks and step budgets raise activation memory by 0.1-2.1 GiB. The report states GPT-OSS rises to 0.1 GiB above its floor, and it acknowledges that 16-24 GB Macs and prompts beyond 32k tokens were not measured. That is a provider-local availability and memory-admission concern, related to T-016 and T-029, and the documented default change is a performance and memory tradeoff. I saw no evidence of a concrete security regression, but the code that applies the new defaults is not in this batch. I recommend a later check that the memory floors and admission still hold, and that the Gemma media ceiling of 512 (mentioned in the report) is enforced.

The longer inter-token tail latency in the engine cells (p99 up to 3x, the report's own wording) could affect stream availability, but that is not a security boundary change.

The documented env vars are not forwarded to LaunchAgents, except that the docs say PREFILL_CHUNK and STEP_TOKENS are forwarded. The code allow-list is unverified here, so the docs may drift from it. No prefix-cache, encryption, TTL or cacheSalt behavior (T-041) is altered. The report says no load arm used repeated prefixes, and that dense Qwen donors now leave recurrent checkpoints every 2,048 tokens instead of 256. This changes checkpoint granularity, not the at-rest exposure; the HMAC naming and TTL are unchanged. Integration should confirm the implementing source matches these docs.
